//: Story Phase 3, chapter 13: The Sharks Smell the Gust. Midday. Shark level follows the flags (data/maps/ship/phase3/main_deck.patch.json 'sharks'): sharks_sighted following, port_impact_seen attacking, grog_spilled swarm, sharks_lured none. Hull breach (16,21), planks (7,32), stern rail (5-14,2), Frog Grog cask (13,23), rowboat (4,24).
p3c5.science: captain[angry]: Garrick. What sharks?
garrick[nervous]: It's only a theory, Captain. A very well-researched theory.
garrick[businesslike]: You'll know a shark can smell a single drop of blood a mile off.
garrick: Well. Imagine what they make of me.
hale[resigned]: Here we go.
garrick: I've made a study of it. Different ingredients attract different sharks.
garrick[proud]: Cheese brings the little ones. Blues. Nippers.
garrick: Garlic draws the hammerheads. It's the shape of the head, you see. Built for garlic.
garrick: Beans bring the big ones.
captain: And eel?
garrick[nervous]: ...Eel brings everything, Captain.
brask[laugh]: Hah! Sharks. There's not been a shark in the Sapphire Sea this time of year since my granddad's day.
rook[laugh]: Built for garlic!
hale: I've sailed these waters for thirty years, Garrick. I've seen two sharks. One of them was a log.
garrick[pretend]: I'm only saying I've been counting fins since the Gust, Mister Hale. Purely for the log.
captain: You've been COUNTING them?
garrick: I've got up to eleven.

p3c5.science.text: FINS! FINS OFF THE STARBOARD QUARTER!

p3c5.science: ned[alarmed]: FINS! Captain! Lots of them! They're all round us!
Fins. Grey, and sharp, and a great many of them, sliding round and round the ship in a slow, patient loop.
rook[alarmed]: ...Sharks.
brask[alarmed]: That's a lot more than eleven.
garrick[nervous]: I did say it was a theory.
hale[alarmed]: Something hit us! Port side, midships!

p3c5.science.tutorial: Something has struck the port side. Get over there and see how bad it is.
p3c5.science.title: Sharks!

p3c5.impact: A shark has its jaws round the port rail. As you watch, it takes a bite out of the hull, chews it thoughtfully, and sinks away.
Where it bit, there's a hole in the planking you could put your head through. You decide not to.
jory[alarmed]: She's holed! Captain, she's HOLED! They're eating the ship!
jory[determined]: I need a plank. There's a pile by the fore hatch. Get me a plank and I'll hold it, you hammer.
jory: And be QUICK about it. They'll be back for seconds.

p3c5.impact.tutorial: Fetch a plank from the pile by the fore hatch, then bring it to the breach. Strike when the marker is in the green.
p3c5.impact.title: Sharks!

then: You've already got a plank. Jory's waiting at the breach.
else: A pile of spare planking, lashed down by the fore hatch. You pick out the least yellow one.
You've got the plank. Now back to the breach.

then: jory[alarmed]: A PLANK, Captain! By the fore hatch! I can't patch it with my hands!

p3c5.patch: jory[determined]: That's it! Hold it there— no, higher— THERE!
jory: Now HAMMER! Hit the nail when it's in the green!

then: jory[happy]: Not one nail bent! That's shipwright's work, Captain!
jory: It'll hold. It's not pretty, but it'll hold.
else: jory[annoyed]: ...It's mostly held on with bent nails and hope, Captain. I'll go over it later.

p3c5.patch: The shark comes back for seconds, gets a mouthful of fresh oak and iron nails, and sinks away looking betrayed.
jory[alarmed]: Captain, if they've been at the hull, they'll be at the rudder. Check the stern!

p3c5.patch.tutorial: Check the rudder from the stern rail, behind the helm.
p3c5.patch.title: Sharks!

p3c5.rudder: You lean over the stern rail and look down at the rudder.
The rudder is still there. So is a shark, with its jaws clamped round the bottom of it, being steered.
It looks up at you. You look down at it. The helm jerks under Nell's hands.

then: You kick the rail as hard as you can. The shark, startled, lets go.
You pull off a boot and hurl it. It bounces off the shark's nose. The shark lets go of the rudder and eats the boot instead.
The shark, looking faintly ashamed, lets go.

p3c5.rudder: nell[alarmed]: She answers the helm, Captain! Just! There's teeth marks all down the blade!
brask[alarmed]: Captain! The Frog Grog cask's slipped its lashings! If it goes over the side, every shark in the sea'll smell it!

p3c5.rudder.tutorial: The Frog Grog cask midships has broken loose. Get to it before it goes over.
p3c5.rudder.title: Sharks!

p3c5.beard_bait: wick[alarmed]: Captain! Captain, that one's... that one's following you.
It keeps pace with you along the rail: stop, and it stops. Move, and it moves. Its nose is pointed straight at your chin.
captain[alarmed]: Why is it looking at me like that?
gristle[alarmed]: It's the beard, Captain! It's following the beard!

p3c5.beard_bait.text: BEARD BAIT! I'm putting it in the log!

p3c5.beard_bait: captain[angry]: Never mind my BEARD! Get to the GROG!
p3c5.spill: The Frog Grog cask is rolling across the deck, trailing snapped rope, straight for the port scuppers.
Too late. The cask bursts on the rail. A great yellow gout of Frog Grog runs out through the scuppers and into the sea.
For a moment, the sea is very quiet.
Then every fin for a mile turns toward the Queen Anne's Revenge.
hale[alarmed]: They're going MAD for it!
brask[disgusted]: Of course they like it. They're the only ones who do.
A shark comes clean over the rail and lands on the deck in front of you with a wet, heavy SMACK.
It stops flopping. It lifts its great grey snout toward you. It sniffs.
The shark looks at your beard. It looks, unmistakably, disgusted.
It flops back over the side, and goes straight back to biting the hull.
captain[angry]: ...I was just REJECTED by a SHARK.
jory[alarmed]: Captain! The patch is holding, but they'll have us in pieces at this rate!
hale[alarmed]: Captain, what do we DO?

p3c5.spill.tutorial: Find Garrick, by his barrel at the mainmast. This is his mess.
p3c5.spill.title: Sharks!

p3c5.solution: You grab the Grand Stenchmaster by the front of his curtain.
captain[angry]: YOU. You brought them.
garrick[nervous]: In fairness, Captain, they brought themselves. I merely... issued the invitation.
captain[angry]: Then you UN-invite them.
garrick[terrified]: Right. Yes. Well. There IS one approach that springs to mind...
garrick[businesslike]: Another release.
squawks[horrified]: NO NO NO NO NO!
captain[angry]: No. Absolutely not. Not on my ship.
The whole ship heaves. Something cracks, deep down, where things shouldn't crack.
You look at the fins, circling closer.
You look at the rowboat, hanging from its davits.
You look at Garrick.
captain[determined]: ...Not on my ship.
captain[determined]: Out there.
garrick[nervous]: Captain?
captain: They follow the smell. So we put the smell somewhere else. A long way somewhere else.
hale[alarmed]: Captain, you can't mean—
captain[determined]: I mean it. Garrick. You get in the rowboat, and you row as far as those arms will take you.
captain: And when you're far enough away that I can't see you...
garrick[surprised]: ...A controlled release.
captain[resigned]: A controlled release.
garrick[businesslike]: That's... actually a very sound plan, Captain. Ugly. But sound.
captain[angry]: Don't. Don't you DARE be pleased about this.
garrick[nervous]: There's just one problem.
garrick: After last night, the tank is empty. I've nothing left to give. I'll need fuel.
jim[sad]: ...I've got beans.
Salty Jim's voice is very small.
jim: A whole pot. From breakfast. Nobody would eat them. They've been sitting in the galley, stewing.
captain: Get them.
jim[sad]: Twenty years a ship's cook. Twenty years keeping beans away from men like him.
jim[sad]: And now we're FEEDING the WEAPON.
garrick[delighted]: Oh, they're still warm!

p3c5.solution.tutorial: Lower Garrick in the rowboat at the starboard davit.
p3c5.solution.title: Sharks!

p3c5.lower: garrick[nervous]: Right. Well. If I'm going, I'm going in style.
garrick: Keep the log for me, Captain. Somebody should write this down.
Garrick is trying to row and eat beans at the same time. He has two hands. The arithmetic is against him.

p3c5.lower.text: I'm a BUSINESSMAN, not an ACROBAT!

p3c5.lower: At first nothing happens. The fins keep circling the ship.

p3c5.lower.narrate: Then, one by one, the fins turn away from the Queen Anne's Revenge, and follow the smell.

p3c5.lower: hale[surprised]: It's working. Captain, it's actually working.

p3c5.lower.narrate: A long way off, a small yellow cloud rises over a small brown rowboat. There's no sound at all.
The sound arrives a good while later: a deep, distant WHUMPF, like a door slamming at the bottom of the sea.
Every shark for a mile makes straight for it.

p3c5.lower: hale[happy]: Clear water, Captain! Not a fin in sight!
captain[resigned]: I hate that it worked.
